thread:
Maya S.: FYI - Customer Claire R. filed an escalation: after yesterday's model rollout customers are reporting subtle changes in tone and length. Not an outright bug but affecting UX. Posting examples and request IDs below. Can ML/Prod help triage? :eyes:

Claire R.: Hey team — we've got multiple support tickets from end users saying replies feel more 'formal' and longer after the update. Small but noticeable for our use case. Sample prompt + two responses attached.

Claire R.: Prompt: `Summarize the following email and suggest next steps.`

Claire R.: Response (before rollout, model v2.1):
```
Thanks for the update. Key points: 1) timeline slipped two weeks, 2) budget remains the same, 3) stakeholder meeting needed. Suggested next steps: confirm new timeline, notify stakeholders, prepare updated milestone plan. Happy to help set up the meeting.
```

Claire R.: Response (after rollout, model v2.2):
```
Thank you for sharing this update. After reviewing the email, I identified the following primary points: first, the projected timeline has extended by approximately two weeks; second, the allocated budget appears unchanged; and third, it will be important to convene the relevant stakeholders to align expectations. Recommended next steps include confirming the revised schedule with the team, drafting a stakeholder communication, and updating the milestone plan accordingly. If you'd like, I can draft the stakeholder message and coordinate availability for the meeting.
```

Maya S.: The customer highlighted two regressions: tone has shifted to more formal phrasing and answers are ~30-40% longer on average. They provided request IDs: `req-8a12e`, `req-8a2f3`, `req-8a9bb`.

Tom Li: Thanks — can you upload the raw request/response payloads (including model version header) or paste the top-level metadata? Need to check `model_version` and `generation_params` (temperature, max_tokens).

Claire R.: Pasted the anonymized payloads in the ticket. Headers show `X-Redwood-Model: open-summarizer-v2.2` and `X-Generation-Params: {"temperature":0.2, "max_tokens":160}`. Before rollout it was `open-summarizer-v2.1` with same params.

Tom Li: Interesting. Same params but different model artifact. Initial look: v2.2 includes a paraphrase-normalization finetune we pushed to reduce hallucinations. Could be affecting verbosity and formality. Sending to bench team to run A/B on a few prompts. :thinking_face:

Ben Ortiz: We need repro steps for support to give customers. Suggested steps: 1) call /v1/generate with same prompt and params against v2.1 and v2.2, 2) collect token counts and compare, 3) diff for stylistic markers. I can draft a concise repro guide.

Maya S.: Claire, can you confirm whether customers are on hosted API or Dedicated? Also are they using Redwood SDK or raw HTTP?

Claire R.: They are on hosted API via our JS SDK. Most affected customers started noticing after the global rollout yesterday at 03:00 UTC.

Aisha Khan: On infra side: deploy-bot shows rollout completed at 2026-03-12T03:02:17Z across regions. No errors in deploy logs. I can pull per-region traffic samples if useful.

Tom Li: I'm running quick diffs now. Early signal: v2.2 tends to prefer full-sentence connectors and offers an extra clarification offer at the end ("If you'd like, I can..."). That matches Claire's samples. Could be a small loss function weight change on brevity during the finetune.

Ben Ortiz: If that is the case, it's a model-level behavior change, not an inference config bug. Options: revert to v2.1 for the service tier, or patch v2.2 with a brevity-promoting prompt/template or use a post-processing trim. Need Product sign-off on rollback risk.

Maya S.: Customer asked for immediate mitigation — short-term workaround acceptable. Claire: would a model override (pin to v2.1) or a post-process truncation be better for you?

Claire R.: Pinning to v2.1 would be ideal; customers want the exact previous tone. Post-processing is okay but not preferred.

Ben Ortiz: @Tom — can we do a fast rollback for the affected tenant(s) only? We have TODO: run canary rollback steps.

Tom Li: Yes, we can route that tenant to v2.1 via routing policy. Steps: update routing rule, redeploy policy (no infra change). I'll prepare the change and post the exact command.

Tom Li: Command (internal):
```
redwood routes update --tenant acme-corp --model open-summarizer-v2.1 --policy override
```
I'll schedule now for 15:10 UTC if no objections.

Maya S.: Please wait 10m — letting Claire confirm with customer.

Claire R.: Confirmed. Do the rollback. Also please capture side-by-side examples and token counts for our customers. They'll want evidence we reverted to previous behavior.

Tom Li: Rolling out tenant override now. Will post verification samples after it's active. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Rollout started for routing override (acme-corp) at 2026-03-12T15:12:03Z.

Tom Li: Verified. Requests for `req-8a12e` replayed against v2.1 returned the pre-rollout phrasing. Token counts: v2.1=72 tokens, v2.2=98 tokens for the sample prompt. Attached diffs.

Maya S.: Great. Claire, can you pass this to the customers and see if the tone/length complaint is resolved?

Claire R.: I'll update tickets now and ask them to validate. Thanks all.

Ben Ortiz: Next steps for us: ML to analyze finetune changes and identify the loss/aux weight change; QA to run a 500-sample style/regression suite; Product to decide whether to patch v2.2 or rollback cluster-wide. I'll own tracking in the incident board.

Tom Li: Quick note for future: add a small 'brevity regression' probe to our pre-release evals (measure avg tokens + formality heuristics). This would've flagged a 35% token increase. Filing an RFC.

Aisha Khan: I'll attach regional latency and throughput once we complete verification — just to ensure rollback didn't affect perf.

Maya S.: Thanks everyone. Claire — please reopen if customers still see differences after the pin. Closing for now but leaving action items open. :thumbsup:

Claire R.: Confirmed customers are happy for now. Leaving one ticket open for follow-up in 24h to confirm no edge cases. Appreciated!

Maya S.: Closing thread (will move action items to Jira).
